key_insight: Post-training quantization can preserve accuracy and perplexity while still changing an LLM’s behavior in ways that conventional metrics miss.
engineering_relevance: For deployment, quantized models should be validated with decision-level behavioral metrics, not just task scores, because moderate bit-width reductions can alter predictions without obvious performance loss.
method: Introduced correctness agreement to measure overlap in correct predictions between base and quantized models.
Compared multiple LLMs across 8-bit to 2-bit quantization schemes.
Analyzed layer-wise attention distortions using statistical and distributional measures.
evidence_signal: Across multiple models and quantization settings, the authors observe behavioral divergence at moderate quantization and non-linear breakpoints at low bit-widths, with query/key projections consistently more sensitive than value/output projections.
watch_item: The new metric adds evaluation complexity, so teams should ensure it is tested on representative tasks and datasets before using it as a deployment gate.
paper_title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
